question: v05
q: Petrol's killing me. How much more am I paying than a year ago?

transcript.answer:
Petrol in the ABS CPI was **13.5% higher in August 2026 than in August 2025**. That is the latest month available. The automotive fuel index rose from 99.49 to 112.95.

- **Rule of thumb:** every $100 you spent on fuel a year ago now costs about $113.50 for the same amount of petrol. If you spend $80 a week, that's roughly $10.80 more a week, or about $560 more over a year.
- **Pattern:** the rise has been uneven. The year-on-year change swung from -7.2% in February 2026 to **+24.2% in March** and +18.6% in April. It then eased to -7.3% in June and -0.4% in July, before jumping back to +13.5% in August.
- **Recent months:** the index fell from 125.29 in March to 91.53 in June, then climbed to 98.40 in July and 112.95 in August. Prices have risen about 23% in two months.

This is the national average, so prices in your city or at your servo may differ. The September figures haven't been released yet.
